$comment: Entity copy sweep allow-list (tests/entity-copy-sweep.spec.ts). 'allow' = justified matches, each with a reason; an entry matches on pattern, optional route (exact, '*', or 'prefix*'), optional workspaces/channel, and 'snippet' (case-insensitive regex tested against the matched text snippet). 'knownLeaks' = baseline of real leaks ('workspace | route | pattern') tolerated until fixed; tighten by deleting entries (the report test lists entries that no longer reproduce). Never move a real leak into 'allow'.

allow.reason: Fresh workspaces have no recorded privacy activity assessment. These closed conditional-law summaries appear only within the Privacy-law scope region, alongside explicit applicability and operating-location review text. The browser test asserts that context and that no law is labelled assessed as applicable. Incorporation does not select a privacy law.

allow.snippet: Six years is not a blanket destruction period for constitutional records, minutes or registers\.|constitutional records do not expire after six years\.
allow.reason: Reviewed CBCA s.20 and OBCA ss.140,145 records guidance distinguishes continuing articles/minutes/register obligations from accounting retention. Constitutional records describes a corporation's constating records; it does not import a society constitution requirement.

allow.snippet: a company, society or other authorized entity may be an incorporator
allow.reason: The catalog displays the BC incorporation-agreement template, expressly limited to an ordinary private BC company. Other home jurisdictions are labelled separately and preparation is gated by supported packet keys. The statement that a society can be a corporate incorporator is part of that labelled BC template, not a universal rule or a society requirement for the active workspace.
